questions.question: Lui-Ngai- Ni is celebrated as a seed sowing festival by the people of ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lui-Ngai-Ni:-**

 
 
• **It is a two-day seed-sowing festival celebrated by the Naga tribes of Manipur, India. **
 
• It is celebrated on the 14th and 15th of February, marking the beginning of the spring season and the new year for the Nagas.
 
• The festival is a time to **celebrate the fertility of the land and to pray for a bountiful harvest.**
 
• The name of the festival comes from three different Naga languages:-
 
 
• **Lui (Mao language): seed**
 
• **Ngai (Rongmei language): festival**
 
• **Ni (Tangkhul language): sowing**
 
 
 
• The festival is celebrated in all the Naga inhabited areas in Manipur, however, the main festivity is hosted alternately at the Naga inhabited district headquarters namely Ukhrul, Tamenglong, Senapati and Chandel.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Ambubachi Mela

 Rongker

• Losar

questions.question: net exports = total exports - _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**total imports.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net exports equal total exports minus total imports. **
 
• This value can either be positive (resulting in a trade surplus, where a nation exports more goods and services than it imports) or negative (resulting in a trade deficit, where a nation imports more goods and services than it exports).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Total Interest: **

 
 
• **It refers to the entire amount of financial remuneration that is earned over a specific period of time for lending money or other resources. **
 
• In the context of savings or an investment, it would be the sum earned over that period of time as a reward for investment.
 
• In terms of a loan, it would be the cost of borrowing that is paid to the lender.
 
 
 
• **Total Income: **
 
 
• **It is the aggregate amount of earnings generated by an individual or business. **
 
• For individuals, total income can include earnings from salaries, investments, rental income, business income, dividends, etc.
 
• For businesses, this would typically be the sum of all sales, before any deductions or expenses.
 
 
 
• **Total Revenue: **
 
 
• **It is a business term that refers to the total receipts from selling a certain quantity of goods or service. **
 
• It's an important part of a company's income statement and is often considered the "top line" figure as it sits at the top of the document.
 
• It's calculated by multiplying the price of the goods or services by the quantity sold.

questions.question: On heating gypsum at _____, it losses water molecules and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**373K**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Gypsum**:-

 
 
• It is also known as calcium sulfate dihydrate (CaSO4·2H2O), loses water when heated and becomes calcium sulfate hemihydrate, also known as Plaster of Paris (CaSO4·0.5H2O).
 
• **This dehydration process typically occurs when the gypsum is heated to a range of 373 K to 393 K (which is equivalent to 100 to 120 degrees Celsius or 212 to 248 degrees Fahrenheit).**

questions.question: Which of the following books was written by Dayanand Saraswati?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyarth Prakash.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Satyarth Prakash:-**

 
 
• **Satyarth Prakash was written by Swami Dayanand Saraswati, the founder of the Arya Samaj. **
 
• It was first published in 1875 in Hindi and later translated into several other languages, including English, Punjabi, and Gujarati.
 
• **The book is a comprehensive treatise on religion, philosophy, and social reform.**
 
• It covers a wide range of topics, including the nature of God, the soul, the universe, and the purpose of life.
 
• It also criticizes many of the popular religious beliefs and practices of the time, such as idol worship, caste discrimination, and child marriage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Kabuliwala:-**

 
 
• **It is a short story by Rabindranath Tagore, first published in 1892. **
 
• It tells the story of Rehmat, an Afghan fruit seller who travels to India each year to sell his wares.
 
• He befriends a young girl named Mini, and the two develop a close bond. However, when Mini's father discovers that Rehmat is a Muslim, he forbids the two from seeing each other.
 
 
 
• **Stray Birds:-**
 
 
• **It is a collection of short poems by Rabindranath Tagore, first published in 1916. **
 
• The poems are a meditation on a variety of topics, including love, nature, and the human condition.
 
• They are written in a simple, lyrical style, and they have been translated into many languages.
 
 
 
• **Gitanjali**:-
 
 
• **It is a collection of poems by Rabindranath Tagore, first published in 1910. **
 
• The poems are religious in nature, and they express Tagore's deep devotion to God.
 
• They are written in a beautiful and lyrical style, and they have been translated into many languages.

questions.question: Which of the following part of Harappan cities was known as citadel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Citadel**:-

 
 
• **The part of Harappan cities that was known as the citadel was the West Side. **
 
• It was typically located on a raised area and was surrounded by high walls.
 
• The citadel was home to the most important buildings in the city, including temples, palaces, and administrative buildings.
 
• It was also the center of the city's defense system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Harappan civilization

 
 
• Harappan civilization is also called as Indus Valley Civilization (IVC).
 
• John Marshall was the first researcher to use the term, ‘Indus Valley Civilization’.
 
• Indus Valley Civilization (IVC) is one of the four great civilizations of the world.
 
• It flourished along the flood plains of Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra.
 
• It was spread across the western part of South Asia that now lies in India, Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• Indus Valley Civilization spread from the year 2500 – 1750 BC according to radio-carbon dating.
 
• The capital cities were Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

questions.question: ________ are a kind of waste disposal system of the cell.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosomes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes**:-

 
 
• These are small, spherical organelles that contain digestive enzymes.
 
• They are responsible for breaking down a wide variety of cellular waste products, including worn-out organelles, food particles, and bacteria.
 
• Lysosomes are also involved in recycling cellular components, such as amino acids and proteins. 
 
• **Lysosomes are a kind of waste disposal system of the cell.**
 
• Lysosomes are essential for maintaining cell health and function.
 
• If lysosomes are not functioning properly, cellular waste products can build up and damage the cell.
 
• This can lead to a variety of diseases, including cancer and lysosomal storage diseases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribosome**:-

 
 
• ** A ribosome is a complex molecular machine that synthesizes proteins from amino acids. **
 
• It is found in all living cells, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic. Ribosomes are made up of two subunits, a large one and a small one.
 
• The small subunit binds to messenger RNA (mRNA) and decodes the genetic code, while the large subunit adds amino acids to the growing polypeptide chain.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**:-
 
 
• **Mitochondria, often referred to as the "powerhouses of the cell," are specialized organelles found in most eukaryotic organisms. **
 
• They are primarily responsible for energy production in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) through the process of oxidative phosphorylation.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles**:-
 
 
• **These are membrane-bound organelles present in all plant and fungal cells and some protist, animal and bacterial cells. **
 
• They're essentially enclosed compartments filled with water containing inorganic and organic molecules, including enzymes.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 148**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 148:-**

 
 
• **Article 148 of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions related to the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG). **
 
• It states that there shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India who shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal and shall only be removed from office in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• The CAG is an independent authority responsible for auditing the accounts of the Union and State Governments, as well as public sector undertakings.
 
• The CAG's reports are tabled in the Parliament and State Legislatures, and play a vital role in ensuring accountability and transparency in the financial management of the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 134:-

 
 
• It​ provides the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme court in criminal cases. 
 
• The Supreme court of India is the highest appellate court in India.
 
• The appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court can be invoked by a certificate granted by the High Court concerned under Article 132(1), 133(1), or 134 of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 160:-**
 
 
• It deals with the discharge of the functions of the Governor in certain contingencies.
 
• It states that the President may make such provision as he thinks fit for the discharge of the functions of the Governor of a State in any contingency not provided for in Chapter II of the Constitution.
 
 
 
•

questions.question: Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi launched the 'Jal Shakti Abhiyan : ______' campaign on World Water Day, 2021. Fill the blank space with appropriate option.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Catch the rain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain:-**

 
 
• Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain campaign on World Water Day, 2021.
 
• The campaign is a **nation-wide water conservation movement aimed at creating awareness about the importance of water conservation and promoting rainwater harvesting.**
 
• The campaign is being implemented in all districts, rural as well as urban areas, of the country with the **main theme “Catch the Rain, where it falls, when it falls”.**
 
• The campaign has five focused interventions:
 
 
• **Rainwater harvesting and water conservation**
 
• **Enumerating, geo-tagging and making inventory of water bodies**
 
• **Renovation of traditional and other water bodies**
 
• **Reuse of water and recharging of structures**
 
• **Watershed development and intensive afforestation**

questions.question: The first seven Five Years Plans gave importance to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Self-Reliance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The first seven Five Year Plans in India gave importance to self-reliance. **
 
• Self-reliance means avoiding imports of those goods which could be produced in India itself.
 
• **This policy was considered a necessity in order to reduce India's dependence on foreign countries, especially for food.**
 
• The first seven Five Year Plans emphasized the development of the following sectors to achieve self-reliance:
 
 
• **Agriculture**: The plans invested in irrigation projects, dams, and agricultural research to increase food production.
 
• **Industry**: The plans focused on the development of heavy industries, such as steel, machinery, and chemicals.
 
• **Infrastructure**: The plans invested in roads, railways, ports, and power generation to support economic growth.
 
 
 
• The focus on self-reliance was instrumental in India's economic development during the first few decades after independence.
 
• The country became self-sufficient in food production and made significant progress in industrialization. However, the policy of import substitution was also criticized for making Indian goods less competitive in the global market.

questions.question: Pushkar Singh Dhami, who became the chief minister of Uttarakhand state of India in March 2022, belongs to _______ political party.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatiya Janata Party**__.

__
 
• ** Pushkar Singh Dhami:-**

 
 
• He is an Indian politician who is the 10th and current Chief Minister of Uttarakhand.
 
• **He is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and represents the Champawat Assembly constituency.**
 
• Dhami joined the BJP in 1994 and quickly rose through the party ranks.
 
• He served as the president of the BJP's youth wing in Uttarakhand from 2002 to 2009.
 
• In 2012, he was elected to the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly from the Khatima constituency. He was re-elected in 2017 and 2022.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Communist Party of India:-**

 
 
• **CPI is a left-wing political party in India. It was founded in 1925 and is one of the oldest political parties in the country. **
 
• The CPI's ideology is based on Marxism-Leninism. The party's goal is to establish a communist society in India.
 
 
 
• **Nationalist Congress Party:-**
 
 
• **NCP is a political party in India. It was founded in 1999 by Sharad Pawar, who broke away from the Indian National Congress (INC). **
 
• The NCP is a centre-left party that advocates for social justice and economic equality. The party's symbol is a clock.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress:-**

questions.question: Which of the following rivers discharge its water into the Arabian sea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Narmada River 

 
 
• Is the longest river of Madhya Pradesh, followed by the Tapti. 
 
• The Source of the Narmada is Narmada Kund which is located at Amarkantak in Anuppur District, Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Narmada is also known as the Rewa.
 
• People from Madhya Pradesh depend fully on the Narmada River, they consider Narmada as the Life Line of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is one of the major rivers in India that run from east to west along with Tapti and the Mahi.
 
• It flows through the states of Madhya Pradesh (1,077 km ), Maharashtra (74 km), and in Gujarat (161 km).
 
• **It discharges its water into the Arabian sea.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahanadi River:-**

 
 
• The Mahanadi river has its source in the Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh, about 6 kilometers from the village of Pharsiya. 
 
• The river then flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. 
 
• The Mahanadi is the third largest river in peninsular India after the Godavari and Krishna rivers. 
 
• It is a major source of water for irrigation, drinking, and hydroelectric power generation in the two states.
 
 
 
• **​Krishna River:-**
 
 
• ​It originates from the Western Ghats range near Mahabaleshwar in the state of Maharashtra.
 
• The Krishna River has a large and very fertile delta, which continues northeast towards the Godavari River region.
 
• The length of the Krishna river is about 1400 km.
 
• The Krishna River has the two largest tributaries, the Bhima (North) and the Tungabhadra (South)
 
 
 
• Ganga river:-​
 
 
• The Ganga is the most important river in India.
 
• It rises in the Gangotri glacier near Gaumukh (3,900 m) in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand.
 
• Here, it is known as the Bhagirathi.
 
• It cuts through the central and the lesser Himalayas in narrow gorges.
 
• At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda, hereafter, it is known as the Ganga. 
 
• The Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar. 
 
• The river has a length of 2,525 km.
 
• It is shared by Uttarakhand (110 km) and Uttar Pradesh (1,450 km), Bihar (445 km), and West Bengal (520 km).
 
• The important left bank tributaries are the Ramganga, the Gomati, the Ghaghara, the Gandak, the Kosi and the Mahananda.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT a Kathak dancer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ananda Shankar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Ananda Shankar:-**

 
 
• **He was an Indian musician, singer, and composer best known for fusing Western and Eastern musical styles. He was not a Kathak Dancer.**
 
• He was the son of dancer and choreographer Uday Shankar and the nephew of sitar player Ravi Shankar.
 
• Ananda Shankar was a pioneer of fusion music.
 
• He combined the traditional sounds of the sitar and tabla with Western rock, jazz, and electronic music to create a new and unique sound.
 
• His music was both innovative and accessible, and it helped to introduce Indian music to a new audience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sitara Devi:-**

 
 
• **She was an Indian dancer of the classical Kathak style of dancing, a singer, and an actress. **
 
• She was the recipient of several awards and accolades, and performed at several prestigious venues in India and abroad; including the Royal Albert Hall, London (1967) and at the Carnegie Hall, New York (1976).
 
 
 
• **Gopi Krishna:-**
 
 
• **He was an Indian Kathak dancer, actor, and choreographer. **
 
• He also studied Bharatnatyam.
 
• In 1952, at the age of seventeen, Gopi Krishna became one of the youngest choreographers in Hindi film history when he was hired to choreograph dances for Madhubala in the film Saqi.

questions.question: Under which of the following articles is the abolition of titles recognised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 18.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Article 18 in The Constitution Of India 1949
 
• ​Abolition of titles:
 
 
• No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State No citizen of India shall accept any title from any foreign State.
 
• No person who is not a citizen of India shall, while he holds any office of profit or trust under the State, accept without the consent of the President any title from any foreign State.
 
• No person holding any office of profit or trust under the State shall, without the consent of the President, accept any present, emolument, or office of any kind from or under any foreign State Right to Freedom.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 19 deals with the six Fundamental Rights. They are:

 
 
• Right to freedom of speech and expression.
 
• Right to assemble peacefully and without arms.
 
• Right to form association or unions or co-operatives.
 
• Right to move freely throughout the territory of India.
 
• Right to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India.
 
• Right to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade or business.
 
 
 
• **Article 20:-**
 
 
• **It grants protection against arbitrary and excessive punishment to an accused person, whether a citizen or a foreigner or a legal person like a company.**
 
 
 
• **Article 17:-**
 
 
• **It abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.**
 
• Article 17 was adopted by the constituent assembly with slogans of “Mahatma Gandhi ki Jai”
 
• The term ‘untouchability’ is not defined in the Constitution or in the Act.

questions.question: Actual growth rate during tenth five year plan of India was _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.6 percent**__.

• ** Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07):**

 
 
• Its duration was from 2002 to 2007, under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh. 
 
• This plan aimed to double the Per Capita Income of India in the next 10 years.
 
• The features of this plan were to promote inclusive growth and equitable development.
 
• It intended for an 8% GDP growth per year.
 
• It aimed at reducing the poverty by half and creating employment for 80million people.
 
• Further, it aimed to reduce regional inequalities.
 
• It also emphasised reducing the gender gaps in the field of education and wage rates by 2007.
 
• The target growth rate was 8.1% while the actual growth was 7.6%.
 
• During the planning period, the highest growth rate was achieved during the 10th five years plan.
 
• Delhi shows the highest growth rate in domestic product during the Tenth Plan.
